why: The document is fine and no reading of it reaches the checks. pdftotext returns a form feed and nothing else; docling wrote 1255 characters of which 1117 are U+FFFD; pdftoppm renders the table rules, the orange header bands and the town seal with not one glyph, so even reading the page image gives nothing. Only PyMuPDF gets the text out, and it warns "cannot find ExtGState resource GS6" doing it -- the file is malformed in a way that defeats every reader the pipeline has. Measured against all 1575 held PDFs, this is the ONLY one where pdftotext yields under 20 words and PyMuPDF yields 50 or more: a class of one, which is why it is an override and not a change to the reader. The durable fix is upstream -- extract this document with PyMuPDF and store the result -- and it retires this row when it lands.

read: Read as a page image; the held OCR is 671 chars. The sheet heads "ANNUAL TOWN ELECTION / MAY 11, 2021" and foots "Registered Voters 1033 / Ballots Cast 93 / VOTER TURNOUT 9.00% / *WRITE-IN". Three contests print rows that do not sum to their own printed TOTAL, and all three are contests with no name on the ballot: "BOARD OF ASSESSORS (One for Three Years) / GWENDOLYN ANN HUBLER* 11 / Write-Ins 2 / Blanks 91 / TOTAL 93"; "AUDITOR (One for One Year) / JOHN TRICKEY* 3 / Write-ins 3 / Blanks 90 / TOTAL 93"; "MODERATOR (One for One Year) / DANIEL E. ROBB* 31 / Write-ins 2 / Blanks 91 / TOTAL 93". Every other contest on the sheet sums to 93 exactly.
why: The record transcribes the sheet faithfully; the sheet does not add up. In each of the three the printed Blanks is exactly TOTAL minus the scattered write-in row, with the named write-in winner left out of the subtraction: 93-2=91, 93-3=90, 93-2=91. The same clerk's form the following year does it correctly -- Pelham2022 prints "RUSTY ROWELL* 14 / All Others 3 / Blanks 82 / TOTAL 99". So the three excesses are the town's arithmetic, not ours, and they are exactly the winners' own vote counts, which is the signature of that mistake. This is unlike the other records this check flags, where the excess comes from a double-counted write-in subtotal or a wrong seat count and the fix is a row in the adjudication ledger. Here there is nothing to correct: changing Blanks to 80, 87 and 60 would make the corpus disagree with the document it cites. The finding stays visible as OVERRIDDEN, which is the right state for a faithful reading of a document that is wrong.
